title: Design, manufacturing and operational requirements
learningObjectives: Identify design requirements
Distinguish safety and commercial constraints
student:
Assigned payload M = {{M}} {{M_unit}}; assigned reach L = {{L}} {{L_unit}}.

The proposed crane handles battery packs of assigned mass M and has assigned reach L. Identify the functional, safety, manufacturing, installation, maintenance and commercial considerations that should influence its design. Name and justify the three requirements you consider most important before production use. Distinguish requirements from evidence that those requirements have actually been met.
instructor: Relevant considerations include payload/rated capacity, reach and swing range, trolley travel, workspace/clearance, positioning accuracy, repetitive duty, inspection, maintainability, traceable lifting hardware, wall/support adequacy, manufacture, installation, downtime and cost. A defensible three-part priority is load-path/strength/stability adequacy, stiffness and positioning, and reliability under the specified duty. Equivalent priorities supported by the operation are acceptable. Listing requirements does not prove compliance; no certification or actual lifting capacity follows from the exercise.

title: Material selection and property evidence
learningObjectives: Select materials by component function
Compare stiffness, strength, fatigue, and manufacturability
student: Recommend appropriate material classes for the boom, brace, pins, mounting plates, bolts, anchors, chain, hook and hoist hardware. Explain which properties matter for each. Distinguish stiffness, yielding, ultimate failure, fatigue resistance, toughness, wear, weldability, machinability, cost and availability. Identify which selected properties or component ratings would require documented evidence.
instructor: Structural-steel classes are plausible candidates for boom/brace stiffness, fabrication and cost, subject to section and grade selection. Pin materials/heat treatment require consideration of bending, shear, bearing, wear, fatigue and toughness. Welded plates, bolts and wall anchors need compatible material/connection and substrate evidence. Hooks, chains and hoists require rated, traceable components; nominal material stress is not a substitute for a component rating. E = {{E}} MPa and sigma_y = {{sigma_y}} MPa are assigned member references, not an identified steel grade or pin specification. Do not infer ultimate strength, fatigue resistance, proportional limit or allowables from those two numbers.

title: Geometry and load path
learningObjectives: Classify system, member, and connection geometry
Explain how geometry affects load transfer
student: Classify the system, member and connection geometry that influences load transfer, stress, displacement, stability, fatigue and connection behavior. Distinguish horizontal boom reach L, horizontal attachment distance a, brace angle theta, wall-anchor spacing h and diagonal brace length ell_b. Explain why a trolley coordinate on a fixed boom is different from changing L. Identify geometric information that the context illustration does not reliably supply.
instructor: System geometry includes reach, trolley position, support coordinates, attachment distance, brace angle, wall spacing, swing and hook position. In the later common model, h = a tan(theta), ell_b = a/cos(theta); a = {{Lb}} m is horizontal, not diagonal. Section geometry includes A, I, S, axes, thicknesses, unsupported lengths and radii; connection geometry includes pin/hole diameters, lug thickness, shear planes, edge distances, bolt spacing, eccentricity and weld details. Load position changes response according to the selected restraints and its interval; do not assume every bending extreme increases monotonically for every inboard load position. The numerical exercise fixes the payload at full reach and does not provide an independent trolley-travel coordinate. The historical image labels are not numerical givens.

title: Loading and the limits of the assigned case
learningObjectives: Estimate design loads
Classify static, dynamic, impact, cyclic, and accidental loads
student: Develop a preliminary loading model for the real handling operation. Identify static, quasi-static, dynamic, impact, cyclic and accidental actions. Distinguish nominal service load, maximum expected service load, maximum credible load and a factored or amplified instructional case. Identify additional masses and operating information required. Explain how the later assigned battery-only numerical case differs from a complete operational loading model.
instructor: Include battery, lifting fixture, hoist/trolley and structural weights; acceleration/braking, swing/side pull, impact/overload and duty history require operational evidence. A project load expression may include those known or researched masses with explicitly justified factors; they have not been assigned here. The later common case uses only W = Mg = {{weight_N}} N and P = gamma_d Mg = {{P_design_N}} N at full reach, with the prescribed horizontal force/couple pair. The {{gamma_d}} amplification and H = {{H}} N are instructional assignments, not validated worst-case operating loads. Missing weights are explicitly omitted in that calculation, not assumed physically absent. Do not mix an estimated project mass into the fixed representative answer without defining a new input case.

title: Critical locations and omitted modes
learningObjectives: Identify critical locations
Separate strength, stiffness, stability, and fatigue concerns
student: Identify potentially critical locations for strength, stiffness, stability and fatigue in the physical crane. Distinguish local wall/connection effects from the internal forces of a chosen boom model. Explain why a critical section or member cannot be selected solely from appearance or one force magnitude.
instructor: Potential locations include boom-to-brace and wall joints, brace and end connections, pins/lugs, anchors/welds, trolley contact, hoist, hook, chain and fixture. Brace compression and thin/slender members require stability investigation; motion includes member, support and connection flexibility; cyclic concentrations occur at holes/welds/contact details. In the supplied pin-root model A has no reaction couple, although actual wall/anchor forces remain important. Bending extrema must be determined from its diagram: rightward maximum at {{right_moment_locations}} and leftward maximum at {{left_moment_locations}} for the current inputs; D or tied locations can govern under changed couples. No complete failure-mode ranking follows from these nominal calculations alone.

title: Assessment criteria and missing evidence
learningObjectives: Define acceptance criteria
Connect calculated responses to allowable limits
student: Identify numerical criteria and evidence that would be needed to assess repeated service, including member yielding, ultimate failure, connection shear/bearing, stability, fatigue, motion, proof-load and rated-load requirements. Distinguish supplied instructional criteria from criteria that cannot yet be evaluated. Do not invent an allowable, material grade, duty life or code requirement.
instructor: The later numerical exercise can compare nominal bending and brace axial stress with the assigned sigma_y/N_y, average pin shear with the assigned {{tau_allow}} MPa, main-lug bearing with the assigned {{bearing_allow}} MPa, and absolute braced tip movement with the assigned {{delta_allow}} mm. These are scoped instructional criteria. No validated compression resistance, combined boom stress, fatigue criterion/history, ultimate/net-section resistance, anchor/wall capacity, proof-test procedure or hardware rating is supplied. The correct response for these missing checks is the required evidence and method to establish it, not an invented number. Met nominal criteria do not prove repeated-service safety.

title: Independent idealization and free-body diagrams
learningObjectives: Create a two-dimensional idealization
Draw complete free-body diagrams
student: Using the context illustration, propose your own two-dimensional structural idealization before looking at the supplied numerical common model. Identify nodes, support restraints and possible force paths. Draw the relevant free-body diagrams and state how the payload, horizontal action and any moment would reach the boom and wall. Explain when the brace could be treated as a two-force member and which effects your model omits. Do not assume a freely suspended chain transmits an independent moment. State what evidence would distinguish your choices from other defensible models.
instructor: Credit an explicit, mechanically consistent proposed model and its limitations, not a guess of the later official layout. A beam boom may carry bending, shear and axial force; an unloaded pin-ended straight brace can be a two-force member. A root pin versus restrained root, wall flexibility, load location and force/couple transfer must be stated. Different defensible choices may be credited for this independent task. A freely suspended chain does not establish a couple-transmitting attachment. The subsequent common model adopts the approved A/B/C/D geometry and prescribed boom force/couple for comparability; it is an assigned model, not proof that the independent model or image has those joints. Completed representative FBDs belong only in instructor output.
gradingNotes: Credit mechanically consistent independent models and stated evidence gaps. The common model is supplied only after I1; no chain-transmitted couple may be assumed without justified load transfer.

title: Establish both signed common-model load cases
learningObjectives: Convert battery mass to design load
Identify moment contributions from vertical and horizontal loads
student: Use the supplied common numerical model. Calculate W = Mg and P = gamma_d Mg. At D apply downward P and analyze H_x = +H and H_x = −H separately, each with prescribed couple C_e = H_x e_H, counterclockwise positive. Draw or label the applied loads for each case and determine their signed moment about A. State which weights are omitted and why the force/couple pair is not a moment transmitted by the illustrated chain. Is PL a reaction moment at A?
instructor:
W = Mg = {{weight_N}} N; P = gamma_d Mg = {{P_design_N}} N. The clockwise vertical-load moment magnitude is PL = {{vertical_load_moment_Nm}} N m. Rightward: H_x = {{right_Hx_N}} N, C_e = {{right_Ce_Nm}} N m, and PL - C_e = {{right_required_brace_moment_Nm}} N m. Leftward: H_x = {{left_Hx_N}} N, C_e = {{left_Ce_Nm}} N m, and PL - C_e = {{left_required_brace_moment_Nm}} N m. The signed applied moment about A is C_e - PL.

A has no reaction moment. The wall anchors and brace equilibrate the prescribed boom loads. Other equipment and structural weights are omitted; the force/couple is not transmitted by the illustrated freely suspended chain. If e_H = 0 the force remains without its couple; if H = 0 the cases coincide.

title: Brace action and complete support reactions
learningObjectives: Apply moment equilibrium to an idealized boom
Resolve brace force components and wall-pin reactions
student: For each M1 load case, use signed moment and force equilibrium of the boom to calculate R_C, F, C_x, A_x and A_y. Use positive F for brace compression and report tension or zero force when the sign requires it. Draw the brace free body and identify the lower-wall reaction. Verify both force balances and moment balance. Do not combine reactions from opposite horizontal-force cases.
instructor:
For each complete case, R_C = (PL - C_e)/a, F = R_C/sin(theta), C_x = F cos(theta), A_x = -(C_x + H_x), A_y = P - R_C. Rightward: R_C = {{right_brace_vertical_N}} N, F = {{right_brace_force_N}} N ({{right_brace_action}}), C_x = {{right_brace_horizontal_N}} N, A_x = {{right_wall_pin_x_N}} N, A_y = {{right_wall_pin_y_N}} N. Leftward: R_C = {{left_brace_vertical_N}} N, F = {{left_brace_force_N}} N ({{left_brace_action}}), C_x = {{left_brace_horizontal_N}} N, A_x = {{left_wall_pin_x_N}} N, A_y = {{left_wall_pin_y_N}} N.

Check A_x + C_x + H_x = 0, A_y + R_C - P = 0, and R_C a + C_e - PL = 0 with unrounded values. On the brace C applies (-C_x,-R_C), B supplies (C_x,R_C). Negative F reverses the compression reference arrows; do not combine reactions from different cases.

title: Braced boom forces, nominal bending and displacement
learningObjectives: Construct signed shear, moment and axial-force diagrams
Compute braced movement with beam and brace compliance
Separate changed-support comparisons from eligible criteria
student:
For both common-model load cases:

  1. Sketch V(x), M(x) and tension-positive N(x) on AC and CD. Calculate the maximum absolute bending moment and every tied critical location; check C and the end couple at D.
  2. Calculate the nominal bending stress M_max/S_boom and its assigned bending-only utilization. Explain what is missing for a combined axial/bending stress and actual stability check.
  3. Calculate signed brace extension, v_C, the boom-bending and brace-axial contributions to tip movement, and their signed sum v_D. Derive or use the stated unit-work relation in the instructor-supplied method brief. Compare |v_D| with the assigned limit. State which compliances are omitted.
  4. Separately calculate the root-fixed P-only cantilever comparison PL, PL/S and PL³/(3EI). Explain why it changes the support model and cannot control the braced assessment or be assumed universally conservative.
  5. Explain one response-specific effect of changing L, I_boom or A_brace, and identify what must be recalculated.
instructor:
On AC: V = A_y, M(x) = A_y x, N = C_x + H_x. On CD: V = P, M(x) = -P(L-x) + C_e, N = H_x. M(A) = 0; M(C) = -P(L-a) + C_e; M(D) = C_e. M_max = max(|M(C)|,|C_e|); M is continuous at C. Rightward M(C) = {{right_boom_moment_C_Nm}} N m, M(D) = {{right_boom_moment_D_Nm}} N m, maximum {{right_boom_max_moment_Nm}} N m at {{right_moment_locations}}. Leftward M(C) = {{left_boom_moment_C_Nm}} N m, M(D) = {{left_boom_moment_D_Nm}} N m, maximum {{left_boom_max_moment_Nm}} N m at {{left_moment_locations}}.

Right/left nominal bending = {{right_boom_bending_MPa}} / {{left_boom_bending_MPa}} MPa; assigned criterion sigma_y/N_y = {{yield_criterion_MPa}} MPa; utilizations {{right_boom_bending_utilization}} / {{left_boom_bending_utilization}}. Axial forces AC = {{right_boom_axial_AC_N}} / {{left_boom_axial_AC_N}} N; CD = {{right_boom_axial_CD_N}} / {{left_boom_axial_CD_N}} N (tension positive). A_boom is unavailable, so N/A +/- M/S and complete boom assessment are unassessed.

Use the supplied unit-work expression. Right/left tensile brace extension = {{right_brace_extension_mm}} / {{left_brace_extension_mm}} mm; C downward movement = {{right_C_down_mm}} / {{left_C_down_mm}} mm. Signed tip bending = {{right_tip_bending_mm}} / {{left_tip_bending_mm}} mm; brace contribution = {{right_tip_brace_mm}} / {{left_tip_brace_mm}} mm. Signed total v_D = {{right_tip_down_mm}} / {{left_tip_down_mm}} mm (right {{right_tip_direction}}; left {{left_tip_direction}}). Absolute-movement utilizations = {{right_tip_displacement_utilization}} / {{left_tip_displacement_utilization}}.

The separate root-fixed P-only comparison gives PL = {{fixed_cantilever_comparison_moment_Nm}} N m, PL/S = {{fixed_cantilever_comparison_stress_MPa}} MPa, PL^3/(3EI) = {{fixed_cantilever_comparison_deflection_mm}} mm. It changes A's rotational restraint; removing the brace with A still pinned would leave a mechanism. It is excluded from the braced ranking and is not universally conservative: the soft-brace counterexample gives greater braced movement.

Omitted compliances are assumptions, not verified zeros. More I_boom reduces only the bending term; more A_brace reduces the brace term. Signed cancellation affects the total magnitude. Changing L also changes the full-reach load position and requires reanalysis.
commonMistakes: Do not substitute cantilever movement for the braced demand, hard-code C as the peak, omit signed brace compliance, mix m and mm, or treat M/S as combined boom stress.

title: Brace and representative connection; critique formal Euler
learningObjectives: Evaluate scoped nominal axial and connection criteria
Distinguish formal Euler arithmetic from physical resistance
Identify unverified axes and load sharing
student:
For both M2 cases, calculate tension-positive brace stress −F/A_brace and its magnitude-based assigned nominal utilization. For the identified brace-end pin/lug, calculate pin area, n_s effective shear areas, average pin shear, full-load lug bearing and their utilizations. State the connection/load-sharing assumptions; do not use F as the upper boom-pin reaction.

Calculate the physical diagonal brace length. For the supplied formal inertia axis compute r_I = sqrt(I_brace/A_brace), K ell_b/r_I and P_E = pi² E I_brace/(K ell_b)². Separately compute K ell_b/r_min using the reported radius and explain the axis discrepancy. Compare the formal Euler stress P_E/A_brace with sigma_y; explain why neither P_E nor P_E/N_b is an established compression resistance. Classify compression-buckling applicability for each signed force case. Identify missing section, restraint and material evidence and at least four additional connection checks.
instructor:
Right/left signed brace stress = {{right_brace_axial_signed_MPa}} / {{left_brace_axial_signed_MPa}} MPa (tension positive); actions {{right_brace_action}} / {{left_brace_action}}; magnitude utilizations {{right_brace_axial_utilization}} / {{left_brace_axial_utilization}} against {{yield_criterion_MPa}} MPa. Pin area = {{pin_area_mm2}} mm^2; total effective shear area = {{pin_shear_area_mm2}} mm^2. Pin shear = {{right_pin_shear_MPa}} / {{left_pin_shear_MPa}} MPa; utilizations {{right_pin_shear_utilization}} / {{left_pin_shear_utilization}} against {{tau_allow}} MPa. Full-load main-lug bearing area = {{bearing_area_mm2}} mm^2; bearing = {{right_bearing_MPa}} / {{left_bearing_MPa}} MPa; utilizations {{right_bearing_utilization}} / {{left_bearing_utilization}} against {{bearing_allow}} MPa. Under equal sharing, double shear halves pin demand, not this lug's bearing.

h = {{wall_spacing_m}} m; ell_b = {{brace_length_m}} m; r_I = {{r_from_I_mm}} mm; reported r_min = {{r_min}} mm. Formal-inertia-axis slenderness = {{formal_slenderness_I}}; reported-radius slenderness = {{formal_slenderness_reported_r}}. {{section_axis_note}}

P_E = {{formal_Euler_N}} N; P_E/A_brace = {{formal_Euler_stress_MPa}} MPa. Divided formal reference P_E/N_b = {{formal_Euler_divided_reference_N}} N. A_brace sigma_y = {{brace_yield_load_reference_N}} N is a yield reference, not column resistance. {{formal_Euler_note}} Compression resistance status: {{compression_stability_status}}.

Only F > 0 demands compression stability; F < 0 needs tensile/reversal evidence; F = 0 has no brace compression demand. Evidence includes actual section dimensions/axes, both restraint directions, material/proportional range, imperfections and an approved method. Pin bending, tear-out, net-section, edge distance, fatigue, wear, clearance, retaining hardware, outer cheeks and B/A connections remain unassessed.

title: Bounded engineering assessment and targeted changes
learningObjectives: Compare utilization ratios
Make a defensible preliminary design recommendation
student:
Using the common-model calculations in M1–M4 (or their equivalent calculations if those tasks were not selected), tabulate the five eligible nominal utilizations for both directions and their envelopes. Identify all tied largest eligible criteria and their controlling cases using unrounded results. State which assigned criteria are met or exceeded and which physical checks remain unavailable. Exclude the changed-support cantilever comparison and formal Euler reference from this ranking.

Recommend at least two response-specific changes or evidence-gathering actions, stating what each targets and what must be recomputed. Do not claim that a single geometry change, a lower raw force or passing these nominal checks establishes overall safety.

Complete this statement: “In the specified idealized model, the assigned nominal criteria are ______. The largest eligible nominal utilization(s) are ______ in case(s) ______. The following physical checks or evidence remain unassessed: ______. The next engineering actions are ______.”
instructor:
Envelope nominal utilizations: bending {{env_boom_bending_utilization}} ({{env_boom_bending_cases}}), absolute braced movement {{env_tip_displacement_utilization}} ({{env_tip_displacement_cases}}), brace axial {{env_brace_axial_utilization}} ({{env_brace_axial_cases}}), pin shear {{env_pin_shear_utilization}} ({{env_pin_shear_cases}}), main-lug bearing {{env_bearing_utilization}} ({{env_bearing_cases}}). Largest eligible utilization {{env_governing_utilization}}; mode(s) {{env_governing_modes}}; controlling cases {{env_governing_cases}}.

{{assessment_text}}

Document section axes/material/restraints for compression resistance; specify the actual pin/lug and inspect bending/tear-out; obtain wall/anchor, duty and rated-hardware evidence. A larger pin can target nominal connection demand, while I_boom and A_brace target different movement terms. Moving a outward or increasing theta is not a universal improvement: geometry, both complete cases, forces, movement, nominal demands and the unvalidated stability question must be recalculated. Formal Euler and the fixed-cantilever comparison do not enter the decision.
